article.title: Register variation in Mandarin: evidence from corpus studies
article.chapter: Norma, estilo y elección avanzada C2 — 規範、文體與進階選擇 C2

claims.summary: Song et al. tagged 88 features in a balanced corpus of 20 Mandarin spoken and written registers and identified five dimensions from 65 features using factor analysis.

On the dimension of explicitness in cohesion and reasoning, academic papers cluster at the positive end, score somewhat below press reviews and essays, and show register-internal variation; official documents have the largest negative score in the reported corpus.
The study identifies a Mandarin dimension of casual real-time speech with stance, whose positively loaded features include exclamations and demonstrative pronouns and mood particles.

Checking genre and purpose before applying register patterns is an editorial inference from the study's multidimensional differences and academic register-internal variation; the study does not prescribe nominalization, impersonality, or specific connectors.
The findings are limited to Song et al.'s corpus, dimensions, and method and do not validate isolated examples or establish a single universal academic/administrative norm.

links.notes: The article's abstract states the sample size, 88 features, 20 registers, factor analysis and five dimensions.
The paper describes academic prose's positive score and internal variation and contrasts official documents' negative score.
The abstract names the dimension and the results interpret its features, including particles and demonstratives, as casual real-time speech with stance.
The study reports different dimensions for academic and official registers and explicitly notes internal variation; the review step is marked as an editorial inference.
The article states the corpus and methodological scope, which does not create prescriptive rules for every discipline or text.
